questions.boundary: The broker boundary around Catalog Management. ecommerce-catalog-service and ecommerce-image-service move from Redpanda to Apache Kafka. The topics they produce (catalog.product.events, catalog.category.events, catalog.attribute.events) move to Kafka with them. ecommerce-product-query-service, ecommerce-category-query-service and ecommerce-tenant-service stay on Redpanda. Every consumer x topic binding between the two sides then crosses the Redpanda/Kafka boundary and has to be bridged by MirrorMaker 2. The image service reading catalog.product.events stays inside the boundary, because producer and consumer both move.

After the move, the catalog service must keep receiving TenantUpdated and TenantDeleted events on Kafka. Those events drive per-tenant DB migrations and deferred tenant cleanup; without them, new tenants get no catalog database setup. The flow redpanda->kafka must carry the topic under the same name (IdentityReplicationPolicy), because the service subscribes to the literal name. The group ecommerce-catalog-service must resume at its translated position (now offset 1). Otherwise auto-offset-reset earliest replays old tenant lifecycle events, or a gap skips new ones.
candidates.ecommerce-category-query-service|catalog: The same catalog.attribute.events mirror also serves the category query service. Its group (offset 20) must keep advancing on the mirrored records, or category attribute joins go stale or get dropped.

CategoryUpdated events produced on Kafka must arrive on the Redpanda topic catalog.category.events (same name, appended after offset 4) with headers and order per partition. The category read model is built only from these events.
candidates.ecommerce-image-service|tenant.tenant.ev: Same as for the catalog service. The image service also runs tenant migrations, and on TenantDeleted it wipes the tenant's S3 prefix through the tenant_cleaners group. A missed delete leaves orphaned objects. A replayed delete is destructive if the tenant has been re-created. The group ecommerce-image-service needs a correctly translated offset on Kafka.
AttributeUpdated events produced on Kafka must arrive on the Redpanda topic catalog.attribute.events (same name, appended after offset 20) with headers intact. The product read model joins master attribute data at query time. A missed attribute event shows stale or hidden attributes on the storefront.

Every ProductUpdated, ProductDeleted and ProductImagePromoted event produced on Kafka by either moved service must reach the Redpanda topic catalog.product.events under the same name. That topic is appended to after offset 120, where the group ecommerce-product-query-service already sits. The flow kafka->redpanda must keep the partition mapping (same partition count), so per-product_id order holds; the projection is version-guarded, but it cannot recover a dropped event. The record headers must survive (event_type is used for deserialization), and so must the payload bytes. Nothing may be produced twice to Redpanda by both the old producers and MirrorMaker 2 around cutover.

candidates: This plan does not establish that the move is lossless or exactly-once. MirrorMaker 2 gives at-least-once delivery at best, so duplicates are possible after a restart. A failure in the cutover window can still lose or duplicate events.

I don't have the runtime Kafka settings of the two moved services: Helm values, the brokers key, group-id overrides, enable-dlq or DLQ topics. R2 was not available. If a DLQ is enabled (default name {topic}.dlq), DLQ topics exist that this plan does not mirror. The exact Helm key that switches the broker is also unconfirmed. The executor must read both values files, and stop if they differ from the assumptions in plan.json.

I don't have partition counts or topic configs (retention, cleanup.policy) for the catalog topics or tenant.tenant.events. R1 shows only partition 0 for each, which suggests 1 partition but does not prove it. The Kafka topics must be created with matching counts after rpk topic describe.

R1 is a snapshot of the consumer groups that are attached now. A consumer that is not running (a stopped job, or another environment) does not appear in it. I also can't rule out a producer outside Catalog Management writing to the catalog.* topics on Redpanda. Such a write would no longer reach the image service after the move.

Offset translation for the groups ecommerce-catalog-service and ecommerce-image-service on tenant.tenant.events is not proven to land at the end offset. MM2 translation can be conservative and re-deliver. Before the services are switched, the executor must check that the Kafka group offset equals the Kafka log-end offset of tenant.tenant.events, and stop if it does not.

To verify after the move: the operator's functional test passes. All of the following are Stable with lag 0 and committed offsets beyond the pre-cutover values (120/4/20): ecommerce-product-query-service on catalog.product.events and catalog.attribute.events, ecommerce-category-query-service on catalog.category.events and catalog.attribute.events. Redpanda log-end offsets for catalog.* grow only through MM2. On Kafka, ecommerce-image-service consumes catalog.product.events, and both moved groups consume tenant.tenant.events with lag 0. A new tenant event reaches both moved services. No topic exists in both allow-lists. No heartbeats topic is ping-ponging.
